checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: Lean separately unfolds the displayed replacement-pair predicate and the displayed applicant-optimality predicate. Neither definition silently receives individual rationality, a vacant-seat block, or an unmatched-applicant block.
checked_proof_steps.scope: This checks the two printed definitions literally. The completed operational reading used by the general Section 4 and Theorem 2 route is kept distinct and is governed by GS62-COMPLETED-STABILITY-READING-01.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Define college-assignment instability by a currently assigned applicant replacing another currently assigned applicant at a mutually preferred college, and define applicant optimality by weak comparison with every stable assignment.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: For distinct finite side types of equal cardinality, every complete strict preference profile has a complete assignment with no man-woman pair who both strictly prefer one another to their assigned mates.
checked_proof_steps.scope: The theorem exposes equal cardinality and the complete strict domain in its type. It does not obtain the result from a same-carrier specialization or from the spelling of a stability predicate.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Run proposer-side deferred acceptance on two finite equally sized communities with complete strict preferences, then use the fact that a rejected proposal was displaced by a more preferred proposal to rule out a blocking pair at termination.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: The direct state records cumulative applications, proves that each round's waiting list equals top-q of old holders union new applicants, preserves disjoint waiting lists and best-first application history, and strictly decreases the finite set of eligible untried pairs whenever an applicant remains active.
checked_proof_steps.scope: This repairs a prior formalization-only audit finding. The earlier cloned-seat sequential stage runner had not been shown to realize the source's within-batch top-q state evolution and could allow a displaced applicant to reapply in a later stage. The published Section 4 algorithm is not classified as defective: source-facing credit now uses the direct exact runner, while cloned-seat machinery is auxiliary comparison support only.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: In each batch, every unmatched applicant with an untried mutually eligible college applies to the best such college, and each college retains exactly its top quota-many applicants from its previous waiting list together with that batch's new applicants.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: The finite untried-pair measure proves termination. At the terminal state the induced assignment is consistent, respects every quota, assigns only mutually acceptable pairs, and has no applicant-college block through either a vacancy or replacement of a lower-ranked assignee.
checked_proof_steps.scope: This proves the Section 4 runner's completed-standard stability directly from its state invariants and terminal condition. Standard stability then implies the separately preserved literal no-replacement condition.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Terminate when every applicant is either held on one waiting list or has exhausted every willing and permitted application, and admit exactly the terminal waiting lists.

checked_proof_steps.checked_conclusion: Every rejected applicant-college pair is impossible in every completed-standard stable assignment, and every applicant weakly prefers the exact terminal waiting-list assignment to that applicant's match in every other completed-standard stable assignment.
checked_proof_steps.scope: The argument starts from the finite strict-list market and the direct source runner, derives the rejection invariant internally, and accepts no possible-college certificate, stable comparison outcome, or optimality conclusion from the caller. Equality with the reusable applicant-proposing assignment is proved afterward from the independently established applicant-optimal stable characterizations.
checked_proof_steps.source_step: Induct over applications and rejections to show that whenever a college rejects an applicant, no completed-standard stable assignment can match that applicant to that college; use this rejection invariant to compare the terminal assignment with an arbitrary stable assignment.

model_conventions.checked_scope: Theorem 1 uses the positive complete-list encoding. The displayed college definitions and Theorem 2 use the incomplete-list encoding with zero as unmatched. The direct Section 4 runner filters to mutually positive pairs before choosing an application, and completed stability excludes assignment to a negative pair, so no paper-facing conclusion assigns source meaning to the relative order among omitted alternatives.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: Lean represents each finite strict preference list by a nonzero injective real-valued score with zero as the outside option. In the complete marriage model every opposite-side participant is acceptable and receives a positive score. In the college model a positive score means listed and acceptable, while omitted alternatives receive arbitrary distinct negative scores solely to make the numerical function total.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source uses finite ordered lists, including incomplete lists in the college model, whereas the reusable matching API takes total real-valued functions. The sign convention preserves acceptability and the score order preserves every listed ranking; making the arbitrary order among omitted negative alternatives explicit prevents that Lean-only totalization from being mistaken for additional source preference data.

model_conventions.checked_scope: The exact waiting-list state exposes only mutually eligible untried colleges to an active applicant. Every new application satisfies the two-sided sign test, and the terminal stability and applicant-optimality results require only the strict-list domain; they have no global applicant-positive-implies-college-positive premise.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: An applicant-college pair is eligible for the Section 4 procedure exactly when the applicant lists the college as acceptable and the college has not eliminated the applicant as unacceptable. In the numerical representation this is the pairwise conjunction of a positive applicant score and a positive college score.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source separately permits applicants to omit colleges they would never attend and forbids applications to colleges that would never admit the applicant. This is a filter on each possible application, not a global assumption that every college acceptable to an applicant must accept that applicant. Recording the pairwise rule prevents the earlier global implication from being smuggled into Theorem 2.

model_conventions.checked_scope: Theorem 2 and its Section 4 procedure route use this reading. The two printed page-10 definitions remain formalized exactly with their literal replacement-pair meaning.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: For the Section 4 procedure and Theorem 2, a stable assignment is quota-feasible and individually rational and has no applicant-college block: an acceptable applicant can block through an unfilled seat or by displacing a lower-ranked assignee. This operational reading does not identify that notion with the earlier page-10 replacement-pair display in isolation.
model_conventions.why_needed: Section 4 says that the terminal waiting lists form the stable assignment and Section 5 compares that outcome with every other stable assignment, while the earlier displayed replacement-pair condition gives only one blocking configuration. Recording the completed operational reading makes the theorem's comparison class explicit without changing or silently strengthening the displayed definition.

reviewed_proof_scopes.semantic_scope: The Section 2 finite strict college-admissions domain, unacceptable alternatives, quotas, the displayed replacement-pair definition of instability, and the displayed applicant-optimality definition over stable assignments.
The finite equal-size complete marriage domain, the prose blocking-pair definition of an unstable set of marriages, and Theorem 1's stable-marriage existence conclusion.
Theorem 1's batched proposer procedure, finite termination argument, complete terminal matching, and rejection-based proof that the terminal marriage has no mutually preferable unmatched pair.

The arbitrary-quota college procedure: mutually eligible applications in applicant preference order, simultaneous new applications by rejected applicants, exact top-q waiting-list updates, finite termination, and stability of the terminal waiting lists.
Theorem 2's comparison of the applicant-proposing procedure with every stable assignment and the induction showing that a rejected applicant-college pair cannot occur in any stable assignment.
